articles.title: Home Assistant prepares apps to run with fewer permissions
articles.dek: New installations change in Supervisor 2026.12; the reduced defaults reach existing installations no later than 2027.05.
body: Home Assistant is reducing the permissions apps receive automatically, limiting what a compromised app could do. Stefan Agner’s new contributor guide asks maintainers to test their apps and explicitly declare any of the four affected Linux permissions they still need.

The change starts with new installations in Supervisor 2026.12. Existing installations keep their current defaults initially, with the reduced set applying to everyone no later than Supervisor 2027.05. Restoring a backup onto a new installation also uses the new defaults.

Maintainers can already test with the optional feature flags in Supervisor 2026.09.3 or newer. The permissions cover raw network access, creating device files, writing to the system audit log and granting executable files extra capabilities. The guide says most apps need none of them. Ping works in the tested Alpine and Debian app images, while custom network tools still need checking.

articles.title: Home Assistant breaks gas use down by device
articles.dek: Separate consumption and flow readings feed a gas flow diagram.
body: Home Assistant’s Energy dashboard adds individual gas devices, so a household with separate readings can see where gas is being used rather than only its total consumption. Each device can have a gas-consumption sensor and a flow-rate sensor.
The accompanying flow diagram connects those readings to the household gas supply. Devices can also identify an upstream device, allowing the view to reflect how the measured gas use is connected.

articles.title: Android Assist listens again after a conversation closes
articles.dek: Two changes address missed wake words when returning to the background listener.
body: Home Assistant’s Android app ends an Assist conversation when someone leaves it, allowing the background wake-word listener to resume. Previously, pressing Home, switching apps or locking the screen could leave the conversation running in the background and prevent the listener from taking over.

A second change prepares a newly created wake-word engine before it receives microphone audio, addressing missed wake words just after the listener restarts. GustavoMorozi contributed both changes, beginning with their first contribution to the Android repository.

articles.title: Home Assistant explains what each helper does before setup
articles.dek: Category filters and searchable descriptions make timers, inputs and calculations easier to find.
body: Home Assistant’s helper picker explains what the available helpers do and groups them into Inputs, Time, Calculations and Other. That gives people a more useful starting point than a long list of names when adding a timer, a calculation or an input to an automation.
The search also matches descriptions and supports keyboard selection. Custom helpers remain available under Other, while the new explanations cover the built-in helpers.

articles.title: Music Quiz plays through the screen hosting the game
articles.dek: A single choice turns a laptop, tablet or television browser into the quiz speaker, including through Home Assistant’s sidebar.
body: Music Assistant’s Music Quiz can use the speakers of the device showing the game. A new “Play on this device” button enables that browser’s web player and selects it, replacing a trip through settings and a search for the browser’s generic player name.

The quiz lists the host’s device first and keeps its audio playing even though browser players are normally hidden. Starting a game also unlocks browser audio on iPhones and iPads. Companion changes identify the browser when Music Assistant is opened from Home Assistant’s sidebar, so the same choice works there.

articles.title: ESPHome simplifies custom connections to wired equipment
articles.dek: Makers can configure compatible serial messages in YAML instead of writing a custom message engine.
body: ESPHome adds a configurable message engine for makers connecting equipment through framed serial buses. It handles the framing family used by Hayward AquaLogic, Jandy AquaLink RS and similar RS485 controllers, moving message assembly, checking and transmission rules from custom C++ into YAML.

Makers define which messages to receive and how to construct commands. The engine checks message integrity and schedules outgoing data around traffic already on the bus. It includes a button platform, but no ready-made device profiles: the equipment’s commands and meanings still need to be configured.
The work is b3nj1’s first contribution to ESPHome.

articles.title: Assist expands everyday voice control in Malay
articles.dek: Timers, music, weather and household status questions join a much wider set of Malay commands.
body: Assist’s Malay sentences expand across everyday household tasks. Zubir Jamal adds timer creation and control, date and time questions, weather, music playback, and commands aimed at a room or floor.

The work also covers questions such as whether a garage door is open or which kitchen lights are on, along with volume, fan speed, covers, scenes and to-do items. Responses use Malay names for device types, colors and fan modes. The sentences include everyday spoken forms, formal variants and familiar loanwords.

pullRequests.title: [ms] Add timer, media, date/time and weather intents
[ms] Add remaining sentences.

articles.title: HomeCore proposes a more consistent Home Assistant interface
articles.dek: The visual foundations are marked complete, and a plan to apply them across Home Assistant awaits approval.
body: A proposal from Matthias de Baat would give Home Assistant a more consistent appearance through HomeCore, a shared set of colors, spacing and controls. The aim is to make the interface feel more approachable for the less technical people in a household.

The implementation proposal moves out of Draft and into Awaiting approval, while the separate visual foundations are marked Done. Matt Beauchamp Buck helped develop those foundations into interface concepts and design guidance.

The plan would apply HomeCore to the default theme, shared components and page spacing, with official theme variables and migration notes for affected custom themes and cards. Navigation and workflows would stay in place. Component records would explain behavior, accessibility requirements and design decisions for contributors; leadership approval is still required before implementation starts.

externalSources.title: Make Home Assistant look like the approachable product we market
Translate visual direction into foundations for Home Assistant

articles.title: Home Assistant’s installer updates itself before the next installation
articles.dek: An Update and restart option checks the download before replacing the running installer.
body: Home Assistant’s desktop installer adds an Update and restart option on its welcome screen. It downloads a newer release, verifies its signature and restarts the installer, avoiding a separate trip to download and replace it manually.

The installer refuses to install an update while it is writing a drive or setting up a virtual machine. Stable installations stay on stable releases; preview installations can move to the same channel or a more stable one.

pullRequests.title: Let the installer update itself from its releases

articles.title: Home Assistant extends timed Powerwall commands to the cloud
articles.dek: Teslemetry’s dispatch and resume actions no longer require local pairing.
body: Home Assistant’s Teslemetry connection extends its timed Powerwall charging and discharging actions to energy sites without a paired local gateway. Those installations send the command through Teslemetry’s cloud connection; paired sites use their local gateway first.
The resume action follows the same route. This opens the timed controls reported in October to cloud-connected installations that the earlier local-only actions rejected.

articles.title: Home Assistant reads Hot Spring water chemistry
articles.dek: FreshWater IQ supplies pH, chlorine and sensor-life readings.
body: Hot Spring spas with FreshWater IQ can expose their water-quality readings through Home Assistant’s integration. The new sensors report pH, chlorine concentration and oxidation-reduction potential, alongside the IQ sensor’s remaining life.
The readings appear only when FreshWater IQ is installed. They extend the spa’s existing temperature and operating controls with measurements of the water itself.

articles.title: ESPHome tunes radio reception for wireless meter readings
articles.dek: An optional radio setting helps compatible receivers lock onto wireless meter signals.
body: ESPHome lets makers adjust how an SX127x radio finds the frequency of an incoming signal. The fixed default was too narrow for some wireless M-Bus meter transmissions, producing damaged data and missed messages before the radio could lock on.

Hajo Noerenberg compared two consecutive four-hour runs on the same ESP32-C3 and SX1276 setup receiving a real meter. A wider correction filter received 50% more messages in that test. The option applies to FSK and OOK radio modes; LoRa is outside its scope.

[sx127x] Document afc_bandwidth option

articles.title: ESPHome steadies pressure readings without a long filtering delay
articles.dek: BMP388 and BMP390 sensors can measure continuously while reporting less often.
body: ESPHome adds continuous measurements for Bosch BMP388 and BMP390 pressure sensors. Previously, heavy noise filtering combined with infrequent readings could take hours to settle, making small pressure differences difficult to follow.

A data-rate setting lets the filter work between reports, useful for measurements such as the pressure difference across an air-conditioning filter. Configurations without the setting retain their existing measurement mode. The work is jda03806’s first contribution to ESPHome.

articles.title: Music Assistant’s metadata update corrects stale library details
articles.dek: An explicit update replaces outdated descriptions and release information while automatic refresh remains conservative.
body: Music Assistant’s “Update metadata” action replaces outdated information instead of only filling empty fields. Corrected biographies, descriptions, labels and release dates can therefore reach items that already have details in the library.

Personal files take priority over streaming services and online metadata sources. If a source cannot be reached, the update only fills gaps, protecting stored information from being overwritten while a music server is offline. Automatic refresh still fills missing fields; genres, artwork and links remain additive, and lyrics are unchanged.
